st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush a 9 x 13 inch baking dish with melted butter.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the spinach in handfuls and cook for 4 minutes until wilted. Squeeze out all the water and cool 10 minutes.
Mix the spinach with the feta, [[2 eggs]], [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Whisk [[1 egg]] with [[0.5 cup]] yogurt for the topping.
Layer 6 sheets of phyllo in the dish, brushing each with melted butter and keeping the others under a damp towel.
Spread the filling evenly, then layer the other 6 sheets on top, buttering each.
Score the top into squares with a sharp knife, pour the yogurt-egg mix over, and drizzle with remaining butter.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet. Brown the lamb in two batches for 6 minutes each.
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper, oregano and garlic. Add [[1 cup]] water and simmer for 40 minutes until tender.
Spread the rice in a baking dish, add the lamb with its juices, and cover with foil.
Bake for 20 minutes until the rice has absorbed most of the liquid.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a pan, whisk in [[3 tbsp]] flour for 1 minute, then remove from the heat and let cool slightly.
Whisk the yogurt, eggs and [[1 tsp]] salt into the flour mixture until smooth.
Pour the yogurt mixture over the lamb and rice.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes until set and golden on top and the lamb reaches 145°F (63°C).
Rest 10 minutes before serving.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and peppers for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and paprika and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Simmer 12 minutes until thick.
Mix the cottage cheese with the egg yolks and the feta if using.
Spoon the cheese mixture over the vegetables and stir gently once to marble it in.
Bake for 15 minutes until set with golden spots. The yolks must be fully cooked.
Serve hot straight from the pan with bread.
Put the beef, lamb, onion, garlic, mint, [[0.5 cup]] breadcrumbs, egg and oregano in a large bowl.
Add [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and mix with your hands for 2 minutes until sticky.
Cover and chill the mixture for 30 minutes.
Shape into 16 small oval or round patties.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and brush with oil.
Cook the qofte for 5 minutes per side until browned and the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with bread, tomato salad and yogurt.
Whisk [[3 cups]] flour, [[2 eggs]], [[2 cups]] milk, [[1 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a thin smooth batter.
Rest the batter for 20 minutes.
Heat a wide nonstick pan or round baking pan over medium heat and brush lightly with butter.
Pour in a thin layer of batter, cook 1 to 2 minutes until just set but not browned, and brush the top with butter and a spoon of cream.
Repeat to build many layers in a stack, buttering and adding cream between layers, until all the batter is used.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Move the stack to a baking dish and pour the rest of the cream and butter over it.
Bake for 45 minutes until golden on top.
Rest 15 minutes, cut into wedges and drizzle with honey.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Mix the onion with the beef, rice, tomatoes, parsley, mint, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper in a bowl.
Fill each pepper about three-quarters full, leaving room for the rice to expand.
Stand the peppers upright in a snug baking dish and put the tops back on.
Stir [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste into [[1 cup]] water with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and pour around the peppers.
Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more, until the peppers are soft and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest 5 minutes and serve with the pan juices.
Put the soaked beans in a pot with [[8 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and boil hard for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Cover the beans with fresh water by 2 inches, bring to a simmer and cook for 60 minutes until nearly tender.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir the tomato mixture into the beans with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Simmer 30 minutes until the beans are creamy and the soup is thick.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] dried mint and taste for salt.
Serve hot with a drizzle of olive oil and crusty bread.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Oil a 9 x 13 inch baking dish with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a skillet. Cook the leeks for 6 minutes, then add the spinach and cook 4 minutes until wilted.
Squeeze out excess water from the greens and let cool for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, yogurt and [[0.25 cup]] olive oil.
Stir in [[2 cups]] cornmeal, [[1 tsp]] baking powder, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper until just mixed.
Fold in the greens and the feta.
Spread in the dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes, then cut into squares.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9 x 13 inch pan.
Beat the egg yolks with [[0.5 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Stir in the vanilla.
Sift [[1 cup]] flour with [[1 tsp]] baking powder and fold into the yolks, adding a splash of milk if the batter is stiff.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, gradually adding [[0.5 cup]] sugar, and fold gently into the batter.
Pour into the pan and bake for 25 minutes until golden and springy.
Whisk together [[1 cup]] whole milk, the condensed milk, evaporated milk and [[0.5 cup]] cream.
Poke holes all over the warm cake and slowly pour the milk mixture over it.
Cool, cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Whip [[1 cup]] cream to soft peaks, spread over the cake, and top with caramel sauce.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Beat [[1 cup]] softened butter with [[1 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Stir in [[1 cup]] cornmeal, [[0.5 cup]] flour, [[0.5 tsp]] baking powder and a pinch of salt to make a soft dough.
Chill the dough 10 minutes if it is too sticky.
Scoop walnut-sized balls onto the sheet, 2 inches apart, and press each flat with your thumb.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden at the edges.
Cool on the tray 10 minutes before moving; they are soft when warm and firm up as they cool.

ing: divided: 2 cups for syrup, 2 tbsp for filling
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Butter a 9 x 13 inch baking dish.
Pull the kataifi into loose strands in a large bowl and toss with [[0.75 cup]] melted butter until coated.
Mix [[2 cups]] walnuts with [[1 tsp]] cinnamon and [[2 tbsp]] sugar.
Press half of the dough into the dish, spread the walnuts over it, then top with the rest and press down firmly.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden.
Meanwhile boil [[2 cups]] sugar and [[1 cup]] water for 10 minutes, then add [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice and cool.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot kadaif, so it sizzles and soaks in.
Let it stand at least 1 hour, then cut into squares.
